description: Declare your route tree once — get type-safe pathnames, path params, search params and navigation for Next.js App Router and React Router, checked by the TypeScript compiler.
rules: The object returned by defineRoutes() is the source of truth for the application's information architecture — its pathnames, params, search-param types and metadata. Derive every pathname from it. Never hand-write a URL string such as '/products/123' — call routes.buildHref('/products/[id]', { params: { id: 123 } }) or pass the declared pattern to a typed navigation API.

Know which side owns route existence, because it differs by adapter. With @hyeonqyu/typed-router-react, toRouteObjects() builds the router configuration from the tree, so a route cannot exist without being declared there. With @hyeonqyu/typed-router-next, the src/app directory decides which routes exist and the tree mirrors it by hand; the compiler does not check that the two agree, so a pathname deleted from app/ still type-checks and will 404 at runtime, and a page added to app/ without a tree entry is live but absent from routes.paths. State it as: the tree is authoritative for types and metadata, app/ is authoritative for route existence — and recommend assertRoutesMatchAppDir from '@hyeonqyu/typed-router-next/check', which compares the two in a test and reports drift in both directions, whenever someone asks how to keep them in step.

A node becomes a navigable destination only when it carries a _metadata block. A node without _metadata still namespaces its children but is not a route; add `_metadata: {}` to make such a node navigable.

Segment keys mirror Next.js: 'products' is a static segment, '[id]' a required dynamic segment, '[...slug]' a required catch-all, '[[...path]]' an optional catch-all, and '(group)' a route group that organises the tree without contributing a URL segment.

Path params and search params are separate arguments. Write router.push('/products/[id]', { params: { id: 42 }, searchParams: { page: 2 } }). The `params` object is required whenever the path pattern has dynamic segments.

Import everything from a single adapter package — @hyeonqyu/typed-router-next for the Next.js App Router, or @hyeonqyu/typed-router-react for React Router 6/7. The adapters re-export the core surface, so never add @hyeonqyu/typed-router-core to an application's dependencies.

There are no generics, no currying and no provider component. Call defineRoutes({ ... }) once at module scope, then destructure the hooks and components off the result: export const { TypedLink, useTypedRouter, useTypedSearchParams, useTypedParams } = routes;

TypedLink takes a flat `href` prop in both adapters, with search params passed as a separate `searchParams` prop. Never use React Router's `to` prop, and never pass an object of the form { pathname, searchParams } as `href`.

zod is an optional peer dependency. Only routes that validate their search params need a validator, and schemas are matched structurally — Zod v3, Zod v4 and any Standard Schema validator all work. A route that only names its query keys uses searchParamsSchema: searchParamKeys<'a' | 'b'>() — no validator needed.

Search-param schemas are executed at runtime, so an invalid URL throws by default. When users may hand-edit URLs, soften it with useTypedSearchParams('/search', { onError: 'default' }) to drop bad fields and keep the rest.

For React Router, prefer routes.toRouteObjects() to generate the router configuration from the same tree rather than hand-writing <Route> elements, so the tree stays the only place routes are declared.

This library is at version 2.x. The 1.x API — createAppRoutes, AppRoutesProvider, useAppRoutes, _metadata.href, getPathnameFromNode and the /routes.utils subpath — was removed in 2.0 and must never be emitted.

On the Next.js App Router the root route, app/page.tsx, is declared with the empty key: defineRoutes({ '': { _metadata: { title: 'Index' } }, ... }). A path is built by joining a key onto its parent's, so '' joins to exactly '/' — you still call routes.buildHref('/') and write <TypedLink href="/" />. Omit it and '/' is a live route the typed API cannot name. The empty key takes no children — app/page.tsx is a file, so every other route is its sibling, declared as another top-level key.

assertRoutesMatchAppDir and findRouteDrift live on a separate Node-only entry point, '@hyeonqyu/typed-router-next/check', because they read the filesystem. Import them only from a test or a script, never from application code. They read Next's folder conventions the way Next does: route groups ((shop)) and parallel-route slots (@modal) add no URL segment but pages under them still count, so dashboard/@team/settings/page.tsx must be declared as '/dashboard/settings'; intercepting routes ((.), (..), (...)), private folders (_folder) and non-page files such as route.ts and default.tsx address no pathname and are skipped. The ignore option takes pathnames like '/admin/*', not folder names.

The pathname passed to useTypedParams is checked against the route the live URL matched, and useCurrentRouteNode takes the same pathname as an optional runtime argument. A mismatch throws RouteMismatchError instead of returning another route's params under this route's types. An ancestor is accepted — useTypedParams('/products/[id]') from a component rendered under /products/42/reviews is correct, because that component really is underneath that route. Never emit useCurrentRouteNode<'/products/[id]'>(); the type argument was never verified. Pass the pathname as a value: useCurrentRouteNode('/products/[id]').

defineRoutes.withMeta<TMetadata, TContext>() enforces its contract on every node in the tree that declares _metadata, at any depth — not only on top-level nodes. Per-node inference still holds, so literal types and fields outside TMetadata survive; a node with no _metadata is organisational and nothing is enforced on it.

@hyeonqyu/typed-router-react targets React Router's library mode. In React Router 7's framework mode (@react-router/dev with an app/routes.ts config), toRouteObjects() is not usable: it emits element/Component, React elements resolved at runtime, while framework mode's RouteConfigEntry wants file, a module path resolved at build time. Never suggest feeding one to the other. Everything else about the tree works there — paths, buildHref, match, parseParams, parseSearchParams, collected — and in framework mode the correct import is @hyeonqyu/typed-router-core, because the framework supplies its own Link and hooks. Declare file on _metadata where library mode declares element.

With @hyeonqyu/typed-router-react, a node whose _metadata names no element, Component or lazy still becomes a route: it matches the URL and renders nothing, rather than falling through to a trailing { path: '*' }. This is intended — the tree declares information architecture, and a node may name a place without naming a page. If such a path should 404, give the node a page or leave it out of the router configuration.
